notes.title: Swedish Language Update
notes.notes:
Big thank you to Erik (VS_Voice) who has done a Swedish translation of Hex Puzzler.

This update also adds globe re-centering and the ability to swap left and right rotation buttons.

Globe re-centering keeps track of the globe's "North Pole" and realigns the globe to the "North Pole" when activated. To activate re-centering, click the new icon in the top left of your screen.

You can now swap the spin and rotate functions on your mouse buttons through the controls settings.

notes.title: Globesweeper Update 1.0.5
notes.notes: This update added Czech language support to the game. As this game requires you to understand complex rules, the Czech language support will help Czech players who do not speak any of the other supported languages. A big thanks goes out to siSINka, who did the translation.

notes.title: Globesweeper: Hex Puzzler v1.0.4 Update
notes.notes:
Version 1.0.4 is now available for Hex Puzzler.

This update greatly improves the in game performance, fixes some visual issues and greatly reduces game loading times.

It is also the 1 year anniversary of Globesweeper so to celebrate Globesweeper and Globesweeper: Hex Puzzler will be on sale from the 17th to the 23rd.

There is a new discord for Globesweeper. Come join us at: https://discord.gg/TySxyCj

[h3]Patch Notes[/h3][list]
[*] New optimised background
[*] Greatly improved game loading
[*] Small graphical fixes
[*] New splash menu
[*] Improved particles
[*] Improved performance on the huge levels
[*] Reduced GPU load
[/list]

notes.title: Globesweeper: Hex Puzzler and my associated spy fantasy
notes.notes:
I have a lot of clicky little games on my phone, and one of them is called Globesweeper, which I got after John (RPS in peace) raved about it at some length. It’s Minesweeper, right, but instead of squares there are hexagons, which tessellate into a 3D sphere. It is very good, and after a few games to get my eye in, I can play it on total autopilot, phased out and thinking about other things.

Now we have a sequel, in the form of Globesweeper: Hex Puzzler. It is more difficult. There’s no autopilot here. Indeed, to play it, I had to imagine I was some sort of a genius spy science wizard. A cross between Bond and M, but like, not one of the rubbish Bonds. Timothy Dalton in License To Kill. Corr, he was a savage, wunee? Oh, and a wizard. I dunno, Gandalf? [pls try harder at wizards Alice – Ed] Anyway, when I played Hex Puzzler, I was Jams Bront, the ultracompetent spy who has a phD and also a flowing white beard.

(more…)
